title: Single element in a Sorted Array
problemStatement: Every element appears twice except one; the array is sorted. Find the single element in O(log n).
intuition: Before the single element, pairs start at even indices. After it, they start at odd indices. That parity flip is a monotone predicate you can binary search on.

approaches.title: Brute: XOR everything
approaches.idea: Correct but linear — it throws away the sortedness.
limitations: Rejected when the interviewer asks for O(log n)

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search on pair parity
approaches.idea: Normalise mid to be even, then compare with its partner.
approaches.whyWorks: Pairs are aligned to even indices exactly up to the single element.

edgeCases: Single element at index 0 or n-1
Only one pair plus the loner
commonMistakes: Not normalising mid to an even index
Using lo <= hi with hi = mid, causing an infinite loop
patternRecognition: Index parity / structural invariants can be binary-searched just like values
followUps: Every element appears three times except one
interviewInsight: If you propose XOR first, immediately add "but sortedness lets us do O(log n)" — otherwise it reads as missing the point.
